unmapped_findings: The real composition of the nominal Fe-8 at.%Al polycrystalline alloy (Table 1) is 7.9 at.% (4.0 wt.-%) Al, with impurity contents C 50 wt.ppm and Si 80 wt.ppm and no other residual elements listed above the reporting threshold. (b0025)

The yield stress of the as-cast polycrystalline Fe-Al alloys increases linearly with increasing Al content up to 18 at.% at room temperature at both compression rates (10^-2 and 10^-4 s^-1); the interpolating straight lines indicate a yield-stress increase of 21 and 23 MPa per unit% for the higher rate and the lower rate, respectively, with Fe-8%Al lying on this line. (b0032)

The solid-solution hardening coefficient reported for the polycrystalline as-cast alloys (0-18 at.% Al) is about 2.2 GPa, in contrast with about 1 GPa reported for monocrystals; the difference is attributed to differences in alloy preparation (as-cast polycrystals vs annealed monocrystals) and slip mode. (b0058)

At room temperature both the strain before necking and the fracture strain show apparent relative maxima at about 8 and 12 at.% Al, which is less pronounced at -100 °C; therefore Fe-8%Al corresponds to a local ductility maximum. (b0040, b0059)
Deformation twinning was observed at room temperature only for the Fe-18%Al alloy and, at -100 °C, for Al contents in the range 11-18%; it was not reported for Fe-8%Al. (b0032, b0064)

The as-cast polycrystalline Fe-8%Al alloy was tested without any subsequent heat treatment; heat treatments reported in the paper apply only to separately prepared samples (e.g. furnace-cooled, quenched), with the as-cast condition serving as the baseline. (b0022)
